text.p: Bonds closed mixed at the longer end but well supported up to the middle of the curve which could feel the benefit on Wednesday of good inflation figures announced for April.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) announced after the market closed that prices rose 1.8 percent year-on-year in April, in line with the more optimistic analyst forecasts, down from 2.5 percent in March.
Some traders said the market could even begin to speculate on a possible further interest rate cut by the Bank of Portugal when it announces money market terms on Friday.
The 10-year cash bonds are already at a record low spread over the German Bund of 76 basis points and could struggle to break below 75, some traders said.
But others noted that a relative lack of paper could push market prices even higher.
"There is a great deal of optimism over our convergence...(but) from here I don't think the spread will narrow much, and there is still the question of the U.S. PPI tomorrow," added another trader.

"Tomorrow there should be interest up to the five years. The inflation figure confirmed the good expectations and people are going to start thinking in a rate cut again on Friday," added said a further trader.
Traders said that the curve was excessively flat and should steepen.
